newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian T-bills open firmer in quiet activity.
newsitem.headline: Canadian T-bills open firmer in quiet activity.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened mostly firmer in quiet trade on Monday with stronger U.S. Treasuries and gains by the Canadian dollar helping to lift prices, dealers said.

"We mostly just tracking along with the U.S. market here," said one T-bill dealer with a bank-owned brokerage. "We're just marking prices up on the back of that. There's a little bit of buying going on but it's a very quiet week. There's not much in the way of data."
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.10 percent from 3.11 percent at Friday's close.
"We are seeing some interest but it's not really heavy. We're getting into the summer season so there's a lot of people away and activity tends to be more muted," said the dealer.
Analysts said the fact that the Canadian dollar has held onto recent gains has also helped to strengthen the money market.
The Canadian dollar opened flat at C$1.3735 (US$0.7280) in heavy trading on Monday after recovering from overnight weakness in overseas markets, traders said.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.36 percent from 3.40 percent on Friday. The one-year T-bill firmed to yield 3.85 percent from 3.89 percent.
The call loan or overnight lending rate traded at 3.20-3.25 percent, near the center of the Bank of Canada's 3.0-3.5 percent target range.
